content.thinking:
I need to plan a complete phoenix design in one pass without testing iteratively—spread wings, standing on talons, with careful attention to keeping it off the ground as specified, while making sure long tail feathers don't awkwardly intersect the floor.

I'm sketching out the joint hierarchy and chains: hips, spine, neck, head, with careful parenting between each bone chain and sizing things to roughly a 3-meter wingspan and 1-meter body height, while keeping the API calls minimal to avoid errors.

Still defining wing joints...

Extruding each feather with its own direction and a gradient paint going from orange at the root to gold/red at the tip, wrapping it in a cel shader based on lit normals to get a faceted look.

I'll mind the atlas cost — each feather gets its own baked paint, around 60 total, but paint cost scales with painted area rather than object count, so that's fine. For bone attachment, primaries rig to the hand/wrist tip joint and secondaries to the elbow/wrist joint, pulling from the chain's joint array (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand).

Now I'm laying out the nine primary feathers per wing, positioning their base points along the wrist-to-handtip line and setting direction angles that sweep from pointing outward near the wrist toward angling backward near the tip, with a slight downward droop increasing outward.

I'm sizing the wingspan to around 4.8m total by setting shoulder, wrist, and hand joint positions and tuning the outer feather lengths down slightly for a more balanced proportion against the 1m body. Now I'm adding the secondary feathers along the elbow-to-wrist segment, angled further back and slightly outward with lengths tapering from 0.8 to 0.7.

I'm layering in tertials from shoulder to elbow and smaller covert rows above the base feathers, then assigning a fire-inspired color palette—crimson, orange, gold, pale yellow—to mimic a Genshin pyro aesthetic with gold trim accents, and considering adding glowing flame-card textures at the wing and tail tips for emissive highlights.

Now I'm placing those flame cards at each wing feather tip, oriented upward with cross-visibility so they read from any angle, then working out how to sweep the body mesh along the spine and neck bone chains from tail to head using a curved path.

Still defining spine and neck paths...

For eyes, I'm placing decals on the skull surface using a surface-hit lookup to position them symmetrically, with gold/orange iris coloring and no blush since this is a bird.

For the head crest, I'm sweeping three curved plumes backward and upward from the head bone using bezier curves with tapered radii and flame-like coloring. For the tail, I'm planning five long streamer feathers that curl and sweep down behind the hips.

Setting up tail bone chain...

radient gradient from crimson at base to gold at tip along the streamer path, and I'm considering adding small golden eye-like discs near the tips using a paint function that colors the top portion of the tail cream and red-gold bands.

Now I'm working out the legs: digitigrade bird legs with talons, using a two-segment limb from hip to ankle to foot, picking hip and ankle target positions and segment lengths so the proportions look right for a bird perched or standing.

Still working out leg structure...

Still tuning toe placement...

Still mapping out foot joints...

Checking the leg distance confirms the hip-to-ankle reach is feasible given segment lengths. Now I'm planning body coloring: gold/cream on the chest and belly, crimson/orange on the back, using toon-shaded fur edges with scattered feather-card textures for breast detail.

Still writing feather card SVG...

Then I'll scatter smaller cards on neck and shoulder mantle, add crown and cheek plumes, and give the wing a tapered sweep tube for the arm bones beneath the feathers. For bone-driven feathers, I'll bind each extrude's `bone` parameter to the relevant joint so they follow the skeleton naturally.

Fixing the orientation: outline width needs to lie in the horizontal plane, not vertical, so I'm computing the cross product of up and the feather direction to get a horizontal perpendicular axis, then deriving the thickness axis from that -- keeping feathers flat rather than standing upright.

Now I'm working out the color painting function for each feather: a gradient from root orange to tip gold, with a pale rachis line down the center and a gradient elsewhere based on position along the feather's length.

Checking that paint propagation works correctly through the outer-to-inner resolve chain with the current context variable, and confirming shading logic for feathers based on normal direction relative to light. I'm also tallying part counts across wing feathers, coverts, and tail to stay under the complexity budget.

Now I'm defining the wing skeleton positions per side—shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip joints with slight dihedral raise—and setting up the bone chain connecting them to the spine for a dramatic spread pose.

Still writing feather outline geometry...

Working out feather angles and lengths...

Still planning feather layout...

I'm planning glow flame cards for wingtips, head crest, and tail tips, each oriented to burn upward from the joint, then sketching the flame SVG with an orange-red outer gradient, yellow mid-layer, and white core.

Finishing the flame SVG at size 128, then adding Genshin-inspired touches: a gold filigree collar, anklets, a circlet with a glowing pyro gem at the forehead, and small gold armlets near the wing joints.

For the chest, I want a glowing orange gem in a gold ring setting, plus scattered ember particles made of tiny merged octahedrons for a sparkly glow effect around the body.

I'm scaling and positioning the embers around the wings with randomized transforms, and sketching overall proportions: head near 1.5 units up, wings spreading to about 4.8 wide, total height around 1.9, standing on talons with wings spread and no base needed.

Now I'm defining the hip root and tail chain positions, sweeping the tail geometry with tapering radii, then laying out seven tail feathers as bezier curves branching from the tail path with varying tip heights.

Still refining the tail curve math...

Still shaping leg geometry and spine width profile...

Still defining body parts...

Still shaping the beak geometry...

Now I'm planning the crest plumes on the head — several feather-like ribbons swept back from the crown, each defined by a base point and curved tip using bezier control with a tapered ribbon radius.

I'm also adding small flame-shaped accent cards at the plume tips for a fiery highlight, colored with a crimson-to-gold gradient, and considering a gold circlet torus wrapped around the head for a crown-like detail.

Rather than risk clipping a full ring against the skull's elongated shape, I'll simplify to a single gem-and-setting ornament placed at the forehead's front-top point, estimating its local coordinates based on the skull's forward and upward extents.

Then for the neck, I'm adding a gold collar ring positioned along the neck chain using its tangent direction to orient the torus properly.

I'll cast a ray onto the chest surface to place a small octahedron gem with a glow effect, backed by a gold cylindrical frame beneath it since a torus would sit edge-on there.

For the wings, I'm adding gold wrist armlets as small tori positioned at the midpoint between elbow and wrist, oriented along that limb's direction, with radius scaling down along a tapering array. Then I'm scattering feather card textures across the body surface, filtering by normal direction to control placement and using two feather texture variants with white tint.

I'm working out the scatter density for neck, body, and tail base feather cards based on surface area and minimum spacing, then checking that the embers geometry (built from octahedrons merged together) has consistent attributes for mergeGeometries to work, and double-checking my imports only include what's actually used to avoid unused-import errors.

Writing color constants and setup code...

Writing plume helper...

I settle on the gradient order: red-to-orange base, then cream, deep, and gold bands by threshold, with a shared paint instance across streamers and cap points locked to gold. Now I'm sketching the feather-adding function signature, pulling in the Joint and Paint types from the skeleton and paint modules.

For the feather body I compute a perpendicular vector to orient the extrusion, build the outline with proper typing, and extrude it with thickness and bone attachment, returning the tip position for flame placement. Then I move to the wing builder, setting up left/right chains with shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand joints parented to the second spine segment, working out where that parent joint actually sits in space.

Checking that the chain parent type accepts a Joint directly, and confirming the arm chain produces four joints matching the span count. I'm sweeping tapered radii along the arm and now mapping feather rows (primaries, secondaries, tertials) to the correct bone segments based on where each span starts and ends, then positioning covert feathers and flame tips with appropriate offsets and color palettes.

Assigning red-orange-gold gradients across primaries, coverts, secondaries, and tertials, and planning small y-offsets per feather index to prevent z-fighting between overlapping layers.

Now I'm computing direction angles for each feather group—primaries angling with slight upward tip curvature, secondaries and tertials at steeper angles with downward dip—then checking the wingspan math works out to roughly 5.2 meters tip to tip.

For the limb helper I'm clarifying that bend directions should be passed as a list containing one direction vector rather than a bare array, since that matches the documented usage pattern. I'm setting up the leg chains with hip, knee, and ankle joints parented to the hips, confirming three named joints gives the right span count including the tip, then sweeping the leg profile with tapering radii and the gold color, reasoning that the hip-to-knee bend will naturally tuck forward correctly even if the thigh is partly hidden inside the body.

Now I'm adding a fluffy pantaloon sphere at the hip and a gold anklet torus positioned partway down the shank toward the ankle, then working out the toe geometry: using the ankle joint as the base point and spreading toe directions at angles like -32, 0, 32, and 180 degrees to place front and rear toes, building each toe as a short polyline swept with tapering radii and a pointed cap at the tip, with a small claw spike extending from the final toe segment.

I'm checking that the claw tip and foot geometry stay within the 2% ground-sink tolerance, adding a gold ball-of-foot sphere at the ankle, then shifting to embers scattered randomly around the scene as small glowing octahedrons in a warm orange tone. Finally I'm setting up the tail chain parented to the hips with tapering sweep radii, and defining streamer ribbons attached near the tail base using bezier curve points, looping through a symmetric range of indices to lay out the outer streamers.

Still writing streamer curves...

Designing the head crest plumes with a fan of ribbons radiating from the head, using a sine-based width taper and a shared red-to-gold paint gradient for the color blend across each feather.

Now I'm sketching the body scatter setup for feather cards, using randomized placement with minimum spacing, and drafting SVG feather textures with crimson-to-gold gradients, central light streaks, and a second gold-cream variant for variety. I'm also setting the eye color to a warm orange and finalizing the type imports needed for the paint mixing functions before returning the completed root.

Now I'm wiring up the chest gem geometry, placing it via a ray hit on the body surface, and estimating total part counts across feathers, cards, and sweeps to make sure the build stays reasonable. I'm also setting up the neck as a chain of joints following a curved path, attaching the head at its end with a forward-and-up direction.

Working through the spike helper for talons, making sure color strings and bone attachments are passed correctly, and checking sweep paint assignments for the tail and ankle torus pieces. Now I'm just going to write the full build using a small vector helper for brevity.
